This website is built from editable **Quarto Markdown** files. Their filename extension is `.qmd`, not `.pdf`, `.html` or `.qml`. A PDF can show an idea, but it is not the file used to maintain this website.

::: {.callout-important}
## What to submit

Submit the edited `.qmd` file and any new image files, or propose the change through GitHub when you have permission. **Do not submit another PDF as the website update.**

For the Bambu Studio guide:

- [open the finished website page](design-fabrication/04-3d-printing/02-slicing-orientation.qmd);
- [view its editable `.qmd` source on GitHub](https://github.com/mrandrewandrade/tech-edu-resources/blob/master/site/design-fabrication/04-3d-printing/02-slicing-orientation.qmd); or
- [download the raw `.qmd` source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrandrewandrade/tech-edu-resources/master/site/design-fabrication/04-3d-printing/02-slicing-orientation.qmd).

Its path inside the project is:

```text
site/design-fabrication/04-3d-printing/02-slicing-orientation.qmd
```
:::

## Choose one route

| Route | Account needed? | Best when |
|---|---:|---|
| **A. Edit locally** | No | You want to use a text editor and give the files to your teacher. |
| **B. Edit with GitHub** | Yes | Parent/guardian permission and teacher or board approval are already in place. |

Both routes edit the same `.qmd` source. GitHub is a way to share and review the change; it is not required to write the page.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Permission and privacy

For this class, **do not create or use a GitHub account without parent/guardian permission and teacher or school-board approval**. The local route works without a GitHub account.

GitHub's Terms require users to be at least 13 years old, and a higher minimum age may apply under local law. Meeting an age minimum does not replace the permission required for this class. Read the [current GitHub Terms of Service](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service#3-age-and-account-requirements).

Never publish your student number, timetable, school account details, private email, location, faces, full legal name or another person's personal information. Ask before including anyone's name or image. A first name and last initial may be used for credit only when the student chooses that credit and the required school consent process is complete.

A pull request is public and displays the contributor's GitHub username and activity. Make a pull request only if you want that public record and all required permissions are in place. A credit line on the finished website is a separate, optional choice. Declining public credit does not affect the contribution or its evaluation.

The [Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario's guidance for schools](https://www.ipc.on.ca/en/media-centre/multimedia-resources/protecting-student-privacy-rights-ontario) says identifiable student information should not be posted online without consent and recommends written consent, or a written record of oral consent, as a best practice. Before adding student credit, the teacher must also confirm the current school and board procedure with the principal or board privacy contact.
:::

## Route A: edit locally with a text editor

### 1. Get a working copy

Ask your teacher for a ZIP copy of the project, or download the repository ZIP only if your teacher has approved that route. Extract the ZIP before editing it.

Open the project folder in an approved text editor. Visual Studio Code is convenient, but a basic text editor can edit a `.qmd` file too. Do not use Microsoft Word because it can insert formatting that breaks plain-text source files.

### 2. Open the source, not the rendered site

Open the `.qmd` file inside the `site` folder. Do **not** edit files inside `site/_site`; that folder is generated again whenever the website renders, so direct changes there will be overwritten.

Keep the file's opening block between the two `---` lines. That is the page metadata.

```yaml
---
title: "Page title"
description: "One-sentence description"
---
```

### 3. Edit with simple Markdown

```markdown
## Section heading

Write an ordinary paragraph here.

- first checklist item
- second checklist item

[descriptive link text](https://example.com)

![Useful description of the image](assets/example.png)
```

Use headings in order, write descriptive link text, and give every useful image accurate alternative text. Keep screenshots tightly cropped and make sure no personal information is visible.

### 4. Save images beside the site's other assets

Put new images in an appropriate folder under `site/assets`. Use short lowercase filenames with hyphens, such as `05-check-printer-profile.png`. Do not rename or move existing files unless you also repair every link to them.

Only add work you made or material the teacher has permission to publish. Record the source and licence for anything created by someone else.

### 5. Preview the page

To preview on a computer with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) installed, open a terminal in the project root, which is the folder containing `README.md`, and run:

```powershell
quarto preview site
```

The terminal shows a local web address. Open it in a browser. Quarto refreshes the preview after a saved change. Stop the preview with `Ctrl+C`.

If software installation is not available on your school computer, you can still edit the `.qmd` source. Give the edited file and its assets to your teacher for rendering.

### 6. Render and check the full site

On the first local setup, install the small Python dependency from the project root:

```powershell
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Then build and check the complete website:

```powershell
quarto render site
python scripts/check_commons.py --rendered
```

`quarto preview site` is the fast working view. `quarto render site` rebuilds the whole website. The check script catches broken links and other project rules. Always run the full render before a change is published.

### 7. Give the change to your teacher

Send or hand in:

- the edited `.qmd` file;
- every new or changed image or asset;
- a two- or three-sentence summary of what you changed and why;
- the result of the render and check, or a note saying the teacher still needs to run them; and
- the sources and permissions for any material you did not create.

A ZIP containing only those files is fine. A PDF is not an editable website contribution.

## Route B: propose the change through GitHub

Use this route only after the permission described above is in place.

1. Sign in to the approved GitHub account.
2. Open the [Bambu Studio guide's `.qmd` source](https://github.com/mrandrewandrade/tech-edu-resources/blob/master/site/design-fabrication/04-3d-printing/02-slicing-orientation.qmd), or navigate to the source file for another page.
3. Select the pencil icon labelled **Edit this file**.
4. If GitHub says it will fork the repository, continue only if that public copy is permitted. A fork is a copy under your GitHub account.
5. Edit the text and use GitHub's **Preview** tab to catch simple Markdown mistakes. GitHub's preview is helpful, but it is not a complete Quarto website render.
6. Select **Commit changes**. Write a short message such as `Clarify Bambu Studio profile check`.
7. Choose the option to create a new branch and propose the change. Do not work directly on the published `master` branch.
8. Open the pull request. Explain what you changed, why it improves the page, how it was checked, and the source or permission for new images.
9. Respond to review feedback by editing the same proposed change. The teacher reviews and decides what is published.

GitHub documents this workflow in [Editing files](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/working-with-files/managing-files/editing-files) and [Creating a pull request](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/creating-a-pull-request).

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Optional: GitHub with a local clone

This route is useful after you have learned branches and commits. It still requires the same permission.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/mrandrewandrade/tech-edu-resources.git
cd tech-edu-resources
git switch -c student/short-change-name
quarto preview site
```

After editing and completing the full render and check:

```powershell
git status
git add site/path/to/page.qmd site/assets/path/to/new-image.png
git commit -m "Explain the focused improvement"
git push -u origin student/short-change-name
```

If you do not have write access to the repository, work in an approved fork and open a pull request from that fork.
:::

## Before you submit

- [ ] I edited the `.qmd` source, not a PDF, Word file or generated HTML file.
- [ ] My change is focused and technically accurate.
- [ ] The steps are numbered, complete and easy for another student to test.
- [ ] Screenshots are readable, tightly cropped and free of personal information.
- [ ] Images have useful alternative text.
- [ ] Links use meaningful labels and open the intended source.
- [ ] I identified the source and permission for material I did not make.
- [ ] I did not edit or submit the generated `site/_site` folder.
- [ ] I previewed the page, or clearly told the teacher that it still needs rendering.
- [ ] I included a short explanation of what changed and why.

## Suggested contribution note

Copy this into your hand-in or pull request and complete it:

```text
Page improved:
Files changed:
Problem I noticed:
What I changed and why:
How I tested it:
New images or sources and their permission/licence:
Credit preference approved by the teacher:
```

## How contributions are used

The teacher may correct, shorten, reorganize or combine a contribution before publication. Educational content on this site is shared under [CC BY-SA 4.0](licensing.qmd), and site code is shared under the [AGPL 3.0](licensing.qmd). Published contributions can therefore be studied, adapted and shared under the applicable licence. A student's name is not placed on the website unless the student chooses public credit and the required school consent process is complete. A student may instead contribute anonymously or use only the public identity already attached to an approved GitHub pull request.
